Hello everyone, been busy with work, hence my absence not that anyone actually missed me, but I missed you guys.

Since we started talking music that relates to LiL, I've recently caught myself listening pretty closely to Vermilion by Slipknot. It did remind me a lot about Akira and Maya:

Her being trapped in a cycle of seeing him fail and die:

She seems dressed in all the rings
Of past fatalities
So fragile yet so devious
She continues to see it
Climatic hands that press
Her temples and my chest

His unusual attraction towards her even devoid of all memories:

She is everything and more
The solemn hypnotic
My Dahlia bathed in possession
She is home to me
I get nervous, perverse, when I see her it's worse


Him embracing his feelings towards her I Will Deliver You To The Fireflies:

Hard to say what caught my attention
Vixen crazy, aphid attraction
Carve my name in my face to recognize
Such a pheromone cult to terrorize
I won't let this build up inside of me

His feeling of guilt and memory (or a memory of a memory) of how their relationship started and what did they turn him into:

I'm a slave, and I am a master
No restraints and unchecked collectors
I exist through my need, to self-oblige
She is something in me, that I despise

...Chapter 4:
She isn't real
I can't make her real


I dunno, maybe it's kind of a stretch on my part, but still, seems to me that it fits pretty damn well.

So, totally random, but on a replay of 'Nothing is Beautiful' by Sel, I've noticed the one girl from the game who hasn't shown up in LiL is Reina, who also happens to be suspiciously similar to Maya.

Reina:
Yuu - "This is Reina. She's probably the most ordinary person I know."
- "She pauses for a second before spinning around and lifting her hand up to the sky."
- "It's a very anime-esque moment."
Reina - "Are you happy here?"

Vs Maya:
Maya - "I'm a normal teenage girl."
- "This is the part of the game where you make it to the rooftop to find the strange girl with her hand pointed up at the sky."
- "Are you happy here?"

Considering that Saki (NiB) seems related to Ami (LiL), and is presumably the grandma that Ami mentions at times, as well as Sensei's mother, the other two love interests of the same game, Miu and Reina may be mothers or grandmothers of certain characters.

Frankly, Reina seemed kind of like a mix of Karin, Maya, and Sana (Sporty, Mysterious, and likes horror movies), and they all happen to have shades of green eyes and in Maya and Sana's case, their colored names are also shades of Green, like Reina's, which makes me wonder if she may be the grandma of at least one of them.

Sara came from a broken home, and it seems likely that Maya did as well, so it might be something that comes up eventually. The Kandas (Karin and Kirin) may be irrelevant, but their father being aware of Sekai seems to imply that their family will play some part in the story.

Otoha also has green eyes like Reina, but there doesn't seem to be any other notable similarities. She seems aware of Sekai though, so there's possibly something there.

Weirdly enough, I didn't feel as bad as I thought I would feel going through the Tsukasa events. Compared to Karin's event, it was quite a breeze.

I mean there were a couple of nail-biting moments in which I felt concerned for Tsukasa's safety and Sensei's sanity, but all things considered, it went pretty well (just gotta wait for the consequences of the choice...)

I think this could be good for Sensei, in a weird way. Remember Maya's words: Sometimes, forcing people to do things they're not comfortable with is the best way to move them forward. This is another part of his past that he needs to confront. We don't know, and he doesn't know the full extent of what happened during his tutoring years, and tutoring Tsukasa might be the key to unlocking those memories.

Tsubasa is either naive (when it comes to Sensei) or a psychopath(in a Sekai-like way), maybe a bit of both. But between trusting her or trusting Sensei, I would rather trust her judgement, and in said judgement, She decided to trust Sensei with Tsukasa's tutoring despite the whole conversation they had...

Of course it could all go to shit and tumbling down if he has a Molly/Karin episode with Tsukasa. But I don't think so, what was happening with Tsukasa felt different. Fingers crossed.

Who knows, maybe even Tsubasa wants that to happen? Actually scratch that about me trusting her judgement, I don't know what the fuck she is cooking

posts.content_html_raw:
There are plenty of subtle things that feel indirect, like pieces you kinda have to try everywhere and see if they fit somewhere:
- To me, the way Pareidolia mentions Sekai disproves the theory of her being the second god/USER2/God of Wires (as well as USER2 being casually referred to as the "/////guy"). But, Kaori transplant theory instead seems to gain one solid support.

- Also, it seems that the sakura tree in the manor is more than just "this tree reminds of someone" now Tsukasa brought up the ghost. Back in Everbloom when Tsubasa first introduced Akira to that room, she threw in bunch of descriptions that sounded foreboding but I was never sure how implying everything was. But perhaps there indeed exists a big secret underneath that soil?


- There has been some girls showing confusion regarding the circular timeline, albeit only Makoto and Tsuneyo experience migraine. I am not sure if this spells a higher possibility of Tsuneyo also joining RAS; but if yes, that means Tsuneyo, Makoto, and perhaps Ayane could have something in common, and that something would exclude Yumi.

These 3 girls have "felt the paranormal" much more directly (canceled suicide, canceled pregnancy, and whatever Tsuneyo is doing), and have remembered things that only happened in the past worlds: Makoto remembering coming to the beach resort and faintly recalling her suicide, Ayane remembering her pregnancy, and Tsuneyo remembering the amusement park date. If this is miraculously onto something, what's left to be solved is the timing of joining RAS (more specifically, why Makoto arrived at the 6th and not earlier) and why these 3 could achieve this and not others.

- Finally, Nodoka's origin. Since Kyoko's name was brought up alongside with Saki, Miu, and Reina, I contemplated on the idea of her being Nodoka's grandma instead of her mother. Perhaps that's why her mom requires more care? That she is much older than the milfs we come to know?

Also since whatever narrator says Nodoka inherits his/its eyes, I suppose it's safe to rule out Sensei as one of the candidate of Nodoka's father since little Akira has gray eyes.

Poor Karin, dude. Holy shit… She didn’t deserve any bit of that. Yet another reason to despise the gods, I suppose. I have to wonder how they’ll handle Karin moving forward

Tsubasa handing out Tsukasa’s number to Akira so readily is… questionable, to say the least. As are her motivations. I’m unsure what she intends to achieve with all this.

I did choose Tsukasa over Chinami last update, so that was pretty lucky.

The Otoha events were fine. I didn’t have it in me to betray Niki and Rin, so I guess I’ll be down a picture message lol. Besides, there’s no way that won’t come back to bite us in the ass later on.

Speaking of Niki, it looks like she’s moving into the house now?? Just… wow... That’s a huge moment if you think about it! Ami needs all the help she can get, anyway. And Akira by extension.

Noriko is such an angel! I loved seeing her be there for Yumi during her moment of vulnerability. Yumi tries to deny it, but I can tell a part of her is grateful for Noriko too.

I think that’s the first time we see Maya actually play the violin if I’m not mistaken! Not only that, but it appears that she misses Sensei badly. It makes me curious how Akira and New Maya’s interactions will go. I would assume not very well, but they gotta talk sometime, right?

It’s cool seeing Io and Uta again. Shame about the cliffhanger on addressing the picture of Uta being on Sensei’s phone, but maybe next time.

…Aaand, yeah, I think that about covers it. Really strong update, but definitely a rollercoaster!

posts.content_html_raw:
Good update, definitely the best for me in chapter 4, it has advanced from best to best

Akira's development is going great, much better so than in 1 2. and in ch3, his development was more or less in drops, so although it was painful, Maya puff was necessary.

The interactions between Yumi and Tsuneyo starting out have a good touch of comedy,
This update is super loaded, with a lot of fourth wall breaking, if you like that you will enjoy it even more, frog boy can enter the ranking of best events in general.

Rain King is super important in this patch

The additions of Better Boy and Frog Boy prove the whole theory of the bad associated with ''Boy'' and perhaps as a counterpart there is now also a ramen Girl

Too many references to the tsuneyo-yumi reset and where you discover more about himawari and like the untitled show, yumi/noriko/akira watched it as children

Noriko has always been an angel of a person here she just solidifies it once again, The only way to not like her is to be in tune with Maya's jealousy.

I don't rule out Akira being the father, because for some reason in this game daughters generally inherit their mother's eye color, so it could be referring to shape or look, or something to mislead. I mean we know about Nodoka's incest fetish, if they are somehow related it makes that plot more spicy.

Damn, 17 on the attack again, a very important number like 23, and it brings back memories of the terminal, and the mall and Amy

In ramen girl there is extensive information about the old toyo, he is now more machine than human, and does the ugly smell continue to decompose even more? It's hard to say that he's not Calm, the blackout again, and as soon as that happens somehow, Tsuneyo loses power and is possessed by some God, which I don't have much idea but I imagine

Luckily I had chosen Tsukasa trying to save chinami, but only a temporary good, in the end it will pass, interesting how the parallelism between Tsukasa/Noriko continues, and how this may be for better or worse in the plot advancement of Akira.

Tsubasa, it is a complicated issue between her Machiavellian maneuvers, to what extent she thinks she does good, and to what extent her means and ends will go. but she is an interesting character among the side caste for sure.

Another detail that interested me more and that no one has talked about was the introduction of a new God Onund, if I wrote it correctly I think, I looked up it and it is something Viking, but for some reason it also reminds me of Onan, son of Juda, biblical Genesis, about masturbation

Tsuneyo Blackout, but associated with Blackout of old district and things from the Coran, interesting, for some reason Akira is also somewhat affected but not completely. the old district adding even more weight, and even Ayane realizing it, but discarding it

Miku's progress was definitely calmer, but with progress and a lot of reference to the possible Thresome with Makoto, and her last event was a rapturous introduction to the main plot of the next patch, a curious nod to the deleted bathroom scene with Miku and Futaba
Augh, disappointingly, I was left wanting a dialogue between Akira and Uta but we will have to wait

Tsuneyo destroying Molly's fantasies by emphasizing her heteroness, I thought she had already done it before or maybe not
Something right with the previews, Tsuneyo remembering more things, and in the end Ayane going to chat about the topic, Makoto goes down a little here I don't trust much after chapter 4, I definitely see more things going wrong with Makoto's new attitude than right and maybe conflicts when new girls arrive at Ras, another plot forming there.

Interesting Niki now moving with Akira, let's see how long it takes for Ami and him to return to a more ''normal'' state, because the Reset should already be close too, and looking forward to seeing Ami's new personality

Otoha is another curious topic, she is not the best in herself, but her arc has greatly improved, compared to past chapters where her only flat function was to be an impediment between Akira and Rin, it is very possible that these nudes will be found in the long run , and drama related to them, and all for ... Otoha number unless maybe this will be awarded later, difficult to know

Maya Violin Scene and music 10/10

In the end REDACTED up 1 affe, what's good Maya events the next patch.

and in the end, damn, again the resource of many millions of affection for the girls who least deserve it, but well the best way to accelerate the plot perhaps, Paranoid enters the top of events to analyze, because it expands much more than what Sekai could have said on Halloween, and all the impersonation between gods, therefore you cannot trust if the god writes in this or that way because it could be someone else impersonating him, which is reliable in this game said in happy in blackout , reliable narrator? Himawari is the closest in wanting to help Akira even so amidst all this upheaval.

There is much more to break down, but this is what brings me back to my memories of having already thought a little about this latest update.

This update was much better than average, in my opinion. I couldn't put it down despite how sleepy I was. Both in regards to characterization and underlying plot developments/reveals.

It was also an eye-opener of sorts. One to some quite apparent things that I still didn't actively realize. Noriko's preciousness and Tsubasa's vileness were skillfully accentuated. I hope Yumi's new friendship works out, and for once, I'm optimistic. Noriko really is that powerful.

From the beginning of Sensei's interactions with Tsubasa, I could sense her twistedness, though initially, I imagined they extended to Touka at most. When the two talked about Tsukasa's tutoring, my worst assumption was being solidified. Perhaps that should have been obvious, with Tsukasa repeatedly and increasingly having questionable dialogues with Sensei.

Having a hunch this kind of development was coming for Tsukasa this update and that it would be foiled by choosing Chinami confirmed my choice.

For a multitude of reasons, Tsukasa was a much easier target.

Regardless, even if something did occur from choosing Chinami, Chika would definitely not stand for it. Maybe she would even kill Sensei, taking her tendencies into consideration. I banked on, however, that my version of Sensei didn't see the bath scene, that he isn't incestuous, and that she's closer to family than Tsukasa. It paid off. Sensei's self-denial when calling Tsukasa was satisfying to see. Showing some real growth there. Fits his new phase of trying to become a better person.

I also thought about the contrasting traits of Maki and Tsubasa despite some of their similarities.
Both have somewhat absent husbands, though Maki's case is more serious. Both care deeply for their daughters (yes, even Tsubasa, in her own twisted way) but fail to properly connect to them. Although much isn't known about Tsubasa, I reckon her sexual inclinations aren't that far off from Maki's. Both were frustrated with that for a long time, for different reasons. We have seen Maki distraught from discovering her daughter was sexually active, despite all her experience, to the point she lost interest in sex. Now we have Tsubasa, who presumably doesn't have much experience due to her upbringing, actively pushing her daughters into these activities. It's interesting.

I hadn't expected Maya and Otoha to mesh so well. That was a surprise. Although you could conceivably predict that if you chanced upon the specific pair, comparing their traits against each other.

Karin's events were excellent, although very sad. Looking forward to developments on that front.

Curious to see how Niki's presence will affect Akira's relationships moving forward.

As for the lore-theoretical side of this update (richly furnished, I'd say), I've noticed some things. Maybe for another time.

posts.content_html_raw:
Some of my ramblings about .38 and other stuff after finishing it earlier tonight:

2nd Yumi event was great, my favorite scenes are like this were Akira actually talks to people.

Loved the violin and Maya staying true, still don't like Otoha and part of me thinks she is just after anything Akira has to one up him/steal from him. Probably just my dislike of her and not actually true, based on the talk they had.

The fucking joke and the Tsunecchi event at the amusement park were also great. I don't really ever understand the more crazy/religious events.

Didn't want to trade the pics, but in my head this would break a 100% and I tried months ago to play without that but it never went very far. I want to 100% since I feel its cannon. I wonder, has Sel said 100% is cannon? I think I remember him saying Akira would always make the wrong choice. If trading them does break a 100%, I will go back through, just like I did with the 3some and Chinami/Tsukasa.

Karin event was rough, cried along with her. I guess something will happen to bring her back into the story. I hope Kirin figures out what happened.

It felt to me that Maya Prime was narrating the end of the last event, she received affection and I could see her saying stop coming to this part of town. Maybe she is one of the narrators?

Pretty much love any event with Niki in it. I feel like Niki wont move in, but she is my other favorite girl besides Maya so I hope it happens. I don't want less Niki, but I kinda want the truth for Chika, Niki, Ami, all of it to come out. Not sure her saying she would stick buy Akira no matter what will be true once she learns all this, or even half of it.

Noriko is a great person and I am glad she helps others out so much. She just was never one of my favorite girls.

I really hope I make it long enough to see the Purity routes.

Thanks everyone again for guides and insights on the events that I can barely understand. Until next month... shit, I work on 4/1. Rats!

I was souring, in fact. So much so that I almost didn't play this update and decided to wait for the next one. To play two in a row and see if things changed. I forced myself regardless, and at some point (fairly early on), I found myself effortlessly blazing through the update, not bored at all.

Definitely felt like the best update in a long time for me. Maybe Selebus had more time to write a tighter package. I don't know. The past few updates were marked by a vacation and an awkward deadline (EOY.) A change of chapter, too.

Or maybe not. Perhaps my humor was better? Maybe I should drink a bit before each update to simulate sleepiness. See if that changes things. Maybe Maya's violin was the cause. That was very soothing.

When I'm sleepy, most of the meandering monologues in this game blur into an indistinct mass of meaning, which I only grasp the surface of before moving on. Usually, I'd try to look into them a bit deeply. Try to tie them together.

Whatever the reason, my interest has been renewed.

Octopuslines said:
Is there a Gallery Unlocker that works? (The one in the Original post breaks this new update for me), I missed the three Tsukasa events, and even if I'm assuming that is a good thing, I want to know what happened there.
Click to expand...
If you know your way of save editing, do the following:
1. Change variables tsukasaspring1skip, tsukasaspring2skip, and tsukasaspring3skip to False
1.1. If you just want to unlock the gallery, simply changing tsukasaspring1, tsukasaspring2, and tsukasaspring3 to True will mark the events completed without actually going through them.

2. Change variables sawchinami and tsukasachosen to True. In addition, change chinamichosen to False to avoid future shenanigans.

3. Call her to trigger the events normally and have your way with the wizard

posts.content_html_raw:
Now after sleeping for 15 hours (Sensei would be jealous), I have just a couple more thoughts about the update

Why did Ami called Niki? was Niki lying? I don't think so. I also don't really think Ami would call Niki for herself. Even if her food was shit, Sensei was a shit caretaker, and Sensei doesn't know anything(non-related to sex) about women, she still wouldn't have called for outside help, for herself.

Most likely that even in her chronically depressed state, she cares about Sensei and knows that he needs help when it comes to taking care of someone. We saw it in that event that it was eating him from the inside not being capable of helping Ami the way she took care of him, and most likely Ami saw that and called Niki not for herself but for Sensei. To help him with this task.

As for why call Niki instead of anyone else, well maybe because she trusts Niki the most. Niki was visiting Coma Sensei and Caretaker Ami all the time with Noriko but never tried to overstep their boundaries


Thought she might still not approve of Niki staying at the house...unless Ami seriously believes this is the best option for Sensei. Even if she is insane, she always does what she believes to be the best for him.

What is Tsubasa's end goal? I have been thinking about that ever since this update ended
And I came with a bit of a twisted theory, which might be possible if Tsubasa is a psychopath, just like Sekai

The fact that Touka loves someone like Sensei, Tsubasa probably considers it a failure on herself for not teaching Touka well enough.

Tsubasa is grooming Touka into becoming the perfect noble lady who will lead the family to a higher realm. Allowing Sensei to infect Touka is a necessary evil. A trial. A vaccine just before Touka enters the world of politics and adulthood.

What would be the best way to cut Sensei from Touka's life in a way that will instill a sense of growth in Touka? to mature and get rid of her "naiveness"? Click to expand...
My thoughts on Ami:
I think Ami did call Niki, and that she's been getting malnourished due to Sensei's, well, incompetence, on top of needing tampons, etc. Niki and Noriko happen to be somewhat family to Ami:
Ami - "Sensei! I have sisters now!"
And even if like everyone else, they are just nice to her to get close to Sensei, they at least seem to want her around. They also are her only real option when it comes to a replacement Caretaker for her and Sensei.

Niki in particular being someone that Ami has noted she'd share Sensei with:
Ami - "You know I love Niki! She's the only girl I'd share you with!"

Sensei's whole "I need to take care of Ami and no one needs to get involved" thing, always felt like Sensei actually just being selfish. It wasn't actually Ami's welfare he cared about. It was about making himself feel better for being a shitty uncle and guardian for who knows how long after having it shoved in his face by Ami breaking right in front of him.

Overall: I'm kind of hoping Ami will move on and quit obsessing over Sensei, once she recovers. I also hope this eats him up inside.

About Tsubasa:
I think she's just bored and seeking thrills by playing with people including her own family. A puppet master flexing the strings of her puppets to have drama. She also seemed sheltered, and desires to see her children have more fun than she did as a kid. As long as that fun is entertaining and authorized by her, anyway.

She likely has cameras watching Sensei with Tsukasa, and would interfere if he actually hurt her, but frankly, I don't think even him fucking Tsukasa would be that big of a deal to her. (Raping her is another story.) They teased the idea of Tsukasa marrying Sensei a few times and apparently everyone sees her as a failsafe.

For now, the Tsukasa tutoring may be comparable to a form of soap opera for Tsubasa. Same might go for the Chosokabes, and whoever Sensei brings to his apartment that she's likely bugged and outfitted with cameras.

Much like how Nodoka once noted Sensei was virtually harmless, Tsubasa has probably came to the same conclusion. He might have the body of a man, but he acts like a child. Simple and predictable. Albeit, their own arrogance may lead to them underestimating him.

I do think Sensei is a form of test for Touka, though. More of a "get it out of your system while you can" kind of thing. However, this probably isn't going how Tsubasa wanted it to go. Instead of teaching Touka about men, Sensei has become like a son to her, and her, a mother to him. Much like how Touka has adopted Yasu, she's virtually adopted Sensei, which I doubt is what Tsubasa expected from this.

Instead of teaching Touka about men, Sensei has become like a son to her, and her, a mother to him. Much like how Touka has adopted Yasu, she's virtually adopted Sensei, which I doubt is what Tsubasa expected from this.

She also seemed sheltered, and desires to see her children have more fun than she did as a kid. As long as that fun is entertaining and authorized by her, anyway.
She likely has cameras watching Sensei with Tsukasa, and would interfere if he actually hurt her, but frankly, I don't think even him fucking Tsukasa would be that big of a deal to her. (Raping her is another story.) They teased the idea of Tsukasa marrying Sensei a few times and apparently everyone sees her as a failsafe.

Finally finished the updated. Lot of fun twists, but the biggest surprise of all?
Mercy. Hope. So early? I was shocked! Tsuneyo proves that Akira isn't the only one who can come back after being reset. Maya can too. Though, for being reset, I can't help but wonder... What's this version of Maya's motivation for hiding her feelings? If she doesn't know about the cosmic weirdness, what's the point in putting on the act? Very curious about her upcoming events in the next update.

Sel really seems to actually want to end the game in our lifetimes. He's moving things along a lot faster these days. Some updates I feel like, while enjoyable and full of memorable character moments, the overall story doesn't advance any. Which is fine to me, as long as it's entertaining, and I think it has been.

Lately, though, every update seems to be moving things along. Not at a sprint, but also not inching. He even had to break the fourth wall to acknowledge he needed to pick up the pace. Very happy with how things are going.

URM offers some more benefits beyond just editing variables. It gives notifications when variables are checked, so you can learn what the consequences are of the choices you made in the past. It also allows choosing options that are locked, so for example, you can currently see some (WIP?) generic events.
Sure, it is possible to do it with console, but you would first have to know that it is possible, which would mean you have to go through the code and see what exactly you need to do in the console to do these things.
I use both the console and URM. I mostly use URM where possible, and console when I'm automating things or edit a lot of variables in a loop (which is not necessary in a simple game like this).

Sure, it is possible to do it with console, but you would first have to know that it is possible, which would mean you have to go through the code and see what exactly you need to do in the console to do these things.
I use both the console and URM. I mostly use URM where possible, and console when I'm automating things or edit a lot of variables in a loop (which is not necessary in a simple game like this).
Speaking of generic events, it is slightly odd to see Ami and Chika look at sensei spending time with someone else, without making a fuzz about it. Especially after the last interaction between Ami and Chika that we have seen.

posts.content_html_raw:
Just finished the new update - since I just started reading the VN, haven't really looked into the sort of supernatural aspect of the series so I can't really comment on that. But yes, I will say that the last several updates has really developed Akira into a truly horrendous human being. Honestly he was actually more palatable at the beginning, where he's barely a human and you're not really even sure if he's capable of things like empathy. But now, it's so much worse because you know that he completely understands how destructive and horrible he is to these girls, and he is constantly reminded of the fact that he is (almost raping Karin (and others), his lust towards little girls, etc). But he still makes no effort to do anything, he keeps making shit choices despite fully understanding the consequences, fully willing to fuck up whatever unfortunate child is in his way. The series is really starting to live up to it's horror tag, and at this point you really start asking if the protagonist even deserves to be saved. Certainly in the real world none of his circumstances would save him from being locked up for a very long time.

I like the series and the characters but with how disgusting the MC is it's starting to get difficult to take any conversation seriously, especially when this guy complains about how sad and regretful he is, when it's like "yeah... but you're still a pedophile rapist who has ruined the lives of multiple girls."

On the brighter side, really liked the scene with Niki. And learned a bit more about Yumi which is always a great thing. Looks like she's friends (?) with Noriko, so looking forward to more interactions between her and the other cast since they always tend to be pretty funny when she's involved. More Otoha development is nice, but I'm a bit disappointed in the direction the story is taking her, since she's starting to feel more like the other characters than different. But we'll see.

I'm totally down with telling fucked up stories, I just really don't see the point of this one. With high schoolers, you can make a point in relation to the genre (which Sel does throughout the series). Almost all VNs are set in high school, and involve a protag trying to romance them. What if we explore the idea of the objectification and fetishization of real life traumas and stories in these sort of games, and try to alter how the viewer experiences these scenarios, a sort of antidote to desensitization? That I can accept - there's an interesting point to be made, and at that stage the game didn't really focus on the MC so he fulfilled the self-insert role most of these stories have.

But with this sort of story, what point are you even trying to make that can't be made using the current cast of characters? And you can't hide behind the idea of "subversion" because your average VN isn't gonna have 8 year old heroines. It also closes far more doors than open because writing wise, adding this element only gives you one real path to develop the character - you don't cross "the line" and get away with it.

But maybe that is the intent, who knows. A litmus test on to what extent the audience can tolerate a monster and at what point will that tolerance break, or how a monster can trick normal people to "empathize" with them. Question is, do you trust Sel enough as a writer to guide the story through, or will we be talking in a few months time how it's not Sensei's fault that Maya or Tsukasa or whoever as a 10 year old tried to seduce him?

I mean, how much of these "good actions" Nodaka does is because of "empathy" and how much of it is because she wants to progress the stories of the characters? Like, I don't know if this is a mischaracterization because I don't really pay attention to her scenes, but it seems like she finds people the most interesting when they're being truest to themselves, good or bad. It also fits in the context of her writing her story about everyone in the class. And honestly, there's kinda no point in bringing up the outcomes when we're considering the intentionality of the character.

For example, you can interpret the scene with Yumi as her getting revenge for Futaba, which certainly was an element, but also an exploration of Yumi's character. Yumi doesn't have a single romantic scene with Sensei, but Nodaka wanted to probe her and confirm if Yumi actually does have feelings for him. That's why Nodoka doesn't do anything with Sensei and just comments on how she didn't expect that if you got the route where Yumi just leaves instead of masturbating to prevent the blowjob. Furthermore, Nodoka doesn't follow through with the blackmail, showing that she was always more interested in Yumi's character and forcing her to progress rather than getting revenge for a friend.

Also, on Kirin, I didn't see the Ayane scene so I can't comment on that, but yes, she's a confused hormonal teen harboring an inferiority complex which she copes with by pretending she doesn't care about anything except sex. And her entire arc is breaking down that act she puts up - in fact, I think the thing with Miku supports this point because you can see how uncomfortable she was. Doesn't help that there's a thirty year old man that's literally her teacher in the room that keeps goading her on and enabling her to keep going down the destructive path.

So yes, Kirin makes shitty choices, but that's mostly because she doesn't understand herself. Nodoka completely understands herself, and every "bad" thing she does is completely justified to her. Kirin is hypocritical, Nodoka is not.

But again, they're all kids and their brains haven't even really developed so I don't blame them. Maybe be a bit more concerned about the grown ass dude who understands how he might accidentally r*pe underage girls but still decides to go on dates and spend time alone with them. It is seen through his own decision-making that r*ping kids is less important to him than his personal satisfaction. If that's not a monster, I don't know what is.

Sensei - "Why is a girl who, at least at this point in time, cites a science fair project and simple familial negligence as her biggest traumas, this far gone?"

Again, I really don't care about what happened, I care about the intentionality. Kirin is a teen with multiple layers of cope hiding her insecurities and makes bad choices because she wants to pretend like she doesn't care about anything. She doesn't actually understand the consequences of her actions because she's a dumb 14 year old. And while it's not good to be stupid, it's a lot more forgivable than fully understanding what will happen and doing them anyways.

On Nodoka, Yumi was already changing before she did her shit, but her feelings towards Sensei weren't changing. Again, in the route where Yumi just walks out, there was no revenge taken besides inconveniencing Yumi, and she doesn't try anything afterwards. It's clear that revenge wasn't the sole purpose, otherwise Nodoka could have made it a lot worse. And sorry, but I don't think Nodoka feels an ounce of empathy for Yumi, so it begs the question why Nodoka didn't make things a lot worse if her only purpose was "revenge."

What did Nodoka actually say that was incorrect? What, that Nodoka should stop doing what she believed as extremely important so Futaba could feel better?

Nodoka isn't evil. There's a quote from somewhere in the game where Sensei describes him and her as two kings sitting on their thrones, and it's a pretty apt description to Nodoka's role. The world is built for Sensei to develop his harem, but the story of the world is being told by Nodoka. And while Nodoka certainly does care about her friends, her greatest priority is telling this story.

Nodoka - "What I'm doing now is closer to solving them. S.A. Nagahara is on a temporary hiatus while I attempt to piece together how and why we are where we are right now."

I've mentioned and showed far more than just "what happened".

Kirin definitely didn't do what she did because she's dumb. Kirin isn't dumb or stupid and she understands the consequences of her actions. She was literally blackmailing a friend, successfully. View attachment 3428865 Kirin - "I'm not asking to be excused. I'm a bad person. I do bad things and then get myself off while thinking about them later on."

Btw, Kirin should be 15 and almost 16 since Christmas is 2 months before her bday. Rin is likely the only 14 year old due to skipping ahead. Funny enough, Kirin should be older than Nodoka.

As for Nodoka, why does it matter if Yumi was changing? If you think Nodoka did this just so Yumi would get sexual with Sensei, you may have missed the part where Nodoka cucked her:
View attachment 3428793 Nodoka - "For tonight only...all I care about is you...all I care about is your huge...huge cock...that I get to have...while Yumi gets nothing...
And they are even further apart from fucking now, than they were. Yumi more or less became a cockblock recently. Revenge also doesn't need to be the sole purpose to still be a major reason why Nodoka did this to her. It's not like Nodoka has done this to anyone who hasn't traumatized and threatened to kill someone close to Nodoka.

There's also no reason for Nodoka to feel empathy or sympathy for Yumi of all people, but Yumi knows better now, and if she'll hurt anyone, it's Nodoka, hence why she's the "Matador" and the event this happened in, was Nodoka's 'Matador' Chapter 3 Event. Nodoka made herself Yumi's target.

Frankly, considering Nodoka could fail to blackmail Yumi, and still end up assaulted if not killed, what Nodoka did was more stupid than what Kirin did. Nodoka was being more stupid than Kirin, when it comes to blackmailing at least. Nodoka's struggle to understand others is way more of a hindrance, than Kirin just being insecure and horny, and petty in Ayane's case. Your point about stupidity being more forgivable should apply more to Nodoka than Kirin.

View attachment 3428703 View attachment 3428704 Futaba - "Or do you think that maybe this will make me a target again?! I'm the easiest one to come after! But we're all going to be fucked!"
- "They're going to hurt me..."

Nodoka's greatest priority also isn't the story, it's making everyone understand (this world), otherwise, her existence means nothing:
View attachment 3428854 View attachment 3428855 Nodoka - "I need to figure out how to make all of you understand."
- "If I can't, my existence means nothing."
As she mentioned in her 'Amoeba (Incontrovertible Peculiarity)' Chapter 3 Event.

"This story" is just a popular work of hers, that she felt inspired to write. It didn't even seem intended to be read by Futaba, or the rest of the class.

She's also literally put her writing profession on temporary hiatus right now:
View attachment 3428934 Nodoka - "What I'm doing now is closer to solving them. S.A. Nagahara is on a temporary hiatus while I attempt to piece together how and why we are where we are right now."
Nodoka has more important things to focus on.

If she was in Ayane's shoes, she would think getting taken advantage of by a cute girl would be great. And again, dumb 15 year old does dumb things, really not that deep.

Nodoka's greatest priority also isn't the story, it's making everyone understand (this world), otherwise, her existence means nothing

Nodoka is a fucking sociopath. She's the one character in all of LiL that if she was written out of the story I wouldn't miss her at all.
Click to expand...
Not contesting the first point, but the second I can't agree with. The story is 100% better with her in it:
1. She gives Yumi a reason to trust Sensei after the unfortunate bridge incident
2. She's even more of a catalyst to Rin's not-so-homie-like attraction to Sensei
3. She's an excellent source of external conflict directed at other girls, so it's not Sensei always filling that role.

If she was a one-dimensional D&D villain whose sociopathy always manifested slasher-film style, I'd agree. But she's a deep and complex character, so brilliant she has little in common with the peers she cannot empathize with. She reminds me a lot of Mia from Californication, only less self-centered. Nodoka is ruled by her desire to experience everything, to better be able to write about it. She may be a sociopath, but without the borderline or disassociative disorders to really turn her into a monster. Instead, she's this giant gray area of amorality that makes her interesting as fuck, if you can get past the way her manic episodes are written.

Edit: Not to mention, Hot/Crazy axis in effect.

I get that perspective, and can appreciate the moral principles involved, but this is a story, not real life. The game would be pretty boring if all the conflict that occurred was Sensei's internal conflict, and his relationships with other characters were 100% positive and pliant. I know there are other harem-VNs out there that use just this conceit, but I find them shallow and trite. Good for a wank, maybe, but I don't really consider it art.

Good stories require conflict (literature 101) and well-rounded characters. No one gets along with everyone, all the time. Traditionally, at least in the west, teenage girls' cliques have been among the most conflict-ridden and cruel peer groups out there. Boys can fight and end up best friends a week later. Girls hold grudges, fight with social ostracism, and are much slower to forgive.

Yeah, I know, arguing that it's important for a harem/horror/fantasy/timefuckery AVN to treat interpersonal relationships realistically is a bold stance, but I'd argue that the VNs that go above and beyond in this respect are the ones that make the longest lasting impression on the reader. Humans are drawn to humanity, so to speak.

posts.content_html_raw:
So, in case anyone was interested about what's going on with the C gods at the moment:
HOPE, The Callous, The Lust Eater, and likely Yasu's god is currently asleep in Underheaven:
Yasu - "But He is asleep right now...and these worthless hands can not find the light on their own."
- "What remains of the fraying rope? And whose are the hands that tug at it while Our Father sleeps in Underheaven?"
Underheaven is likely the same thing as the Bottom of Everything where HOPE seems to reside.

USER2, The Wire god, and The Calm, has apparently just clawed it's way out from where ever it has been since presumably Chapter 2:
It seemed to disappear around the end of Chapter 2, seemingly around the time when Sensei lost the ability to talk to John. It's secret reappearance in Chapter 4, is followed by Tsuneyo walking around Naked.

Pareidolia, USER3, The Dark, and The Concerned is currently connected to Sensei, and presumably has been since near the end of Chapter 3 when we have to connect to it:
Pareidolia(?) - "pareidolia would like to connect."
- "will you allow it?"
It's the one who talked about the illusions of freedom, the flower blooming, and complications, etc:
Pareidolia - "in me, this new world you have found yourself in will truly be your own --- and the illusions of freedom that the others have shown you will evaporate into nothingness."
- "with the coming of the springtime, the ice will thaw and the heat will disappear."
- "and the frozen flower beside you blooms anew."
- "and with those things comes a slew of new complications."
It seems to be the one responsible for most things since Halloween at the end of Chapter 3, and is presumably the strongest god at the moment considering it's spring, and it seems to consider Chapter 4, it's Chapter:
Pareidolia - "Who's going to want to fuck you if all you can do is sit there and feel sorry for yourself? Because I'll be damned if you turn my chapter into some sappy, abstinent romp through an ocean of your tears."

fdsasdf_p said:
A question from 0.38 update: Why does frog boy remind roadkilled Ami of rain king?
Putting whatever the name frog boy is insinuating aside, Rain King is confusing, but somewhat also gives a "supposed to be important" feeling. But replaying it again yields zero frog in the search.

So is there an in-universe connection between them? Or is this just Selly purposefully breaking walls and mentioning all the unexplainable events he made in the past and enjoying himself a circle jerk?

also in my head I kept say fuck boy instead of frog boy
Click to expand...
If I were to guess, Special Ami is saying "frog boy" reminds her of the title "Rain King", more so than the event. Sensei may be intended to be the Rain King but has been acting like a Frog boy instead.

Pareidolia also recently brought up a "mother frog":
"do you have any idea how hard i had to work to get here? how long i had to wait? because i can guarantee you it would make the watermelon girl look like a tadpole gobbled up by its mother frog."
And may actually just be using this Special Ami in Yumi's Chapter 4 'Frog boy' event, as a cover, considering she suddenly talks in lower case:
Special Ami - "You don't have to understand anything!"
- "you just have to believe"

Pareidolia might be using Ami's image, due to Sensei trusting and loving her, which makes it easier to manipulate him, through her. Albeit, that's just a theory at the moment. It may also be manipulating Ami as well:
Ami - "There are a million girls trying to trick you into believing we're not meant to be together, but I have talked to God and he says that we are."

The 'Rain King' and 'Amy' Happy Events seem to be it's Happy Events, considering the context around them. Probably also the 'Second Sun' Happy Event, considering Long Maya mentions frogs and rain:
Long Maya - "The frogs stuck in your throat."
- "It's raining outside."
Plus Long Maya also seems to be trying to make Sensei and Us question things:
Long Maya - "But as you harken back to prior experiences you may or may not have had, you'll come to find that the pieces don't quite fit."
Which seems textbook Pareidolia.

Overall: The connection seems to just revolve around Pareidolia and it's logic.

HOPE, The Callous, The Lust Eater, and likely Yasu's god is currently asleep in Underheaven:

Underheaven is likely the same thing as the Bottom of Everything where HOPE seems to reside.

USER2, The Wire god, and The Calm, has apparently just clawed it's way out from where ever it has been since presumably Chapter 2:
View attachment 3445744 View attachment 3445748
It seemed to disappear around the end of Chapter 2, seemingly around the time when Sensei lost the ability to talk to John. It's secret reappearance in Chapter 4, is followed by Tsuneyo walking around Naked.

Pareidolia, USER3, The Dark, and The Concerned is currently connected to Sensei, and presumably has been since near the end of Chapter 3 when we have to connect to it:
View attachment 3445755 View attachment 3445756 Pareidolia(?) - "pareidolia would like to connect."
- "will you allow it?"
It's the one who talked about the illusions of freedom, the flower blooming, and complications, etc:
View attachment 3445783 View attachment 3445784 View attachment 3445785 View attachment 3445786 Pareidolia - "in me, this new world you have found yourself in will truly be your own --- and the illusions of freedom that the others have shown you will evaporate into nothingness."
- "with the coming of the springtime, the ice will thaw and the heat will disappear."
- "and the frozen flower beside you blooms anew."
- "and with those things comes a slew of new complications."
It seems to be the one responsible for most things since Halloween at the end of Chapter 3, and is presumably the strongest god at the moment considering it's spring, and it seems to consider Chapter 4, it's Chapter:
View attachment 3445823 Pareidolia - "Who's going to want to fuck you if all you can do is sit there and feel sorry for yourself? Because I'll be damned if you turn my chapter into some sappy, abstinent romp through an ocean of your tears."


If I were to guess, Special Ami is saying "frog boy" reminds her of the title "Rain King", more so than the event. Sensei may be intended to be the Rain King but has been acting like a Frog boy instead.

Pareidolia also recently brought up a "mother frog":
View attachment 3445964 "do you have any idea how hard i had to work to get here? how long i had to wait? because i can guarantee you it would make the watermelon girl look like a tadpole gobbled up by its mother frog."
And may actually just be using this Special Ami in Yumi's Chapter 4 'Frog boy' event, as a cover, considering she suddenly talks in lower case:
View attachment 3445968 View attachment 3445969 Special Ami - "You don't have to understand anything!"
- "you just have to believe"

Pareidolia might be using Ami's image, due to Sensei trusting and loving her, which makes it easier to manipulate him, through her. Albeit, that's just a theory at the moment. It may also be manipulating Ami as well:
View attachment 3445971 Ami - "There are a million girls trying to trick you into believing we're not meant to be together, but I have talked to God and he says that we are."

The 'Rain King' and 'Amy' Happy Events seem to be it's Happy Events, considering the context around them. Probably also the 'Second Sun' Happy Event, considering Long Maya mentions frogs and rain:
View attachment 3446021 View attachment 3446026 Long Maya - "The frogs stuck in your throat."
- "It's raining outside."
Plus Long Maya also seems to be trying to make Sensei and Us question things:
View attachment 3446032 Long Maya - "But as you harken back to prior experiences you may or may not have had, you'll come to find that the pieces don't quite fit."
Which seems textbook Pareidolia.

Overall: The connection seems to just revolve around Pareidolia and it's logic.
Click to expand...
After a night of thinking, the only thing that is more certain to me (which you also already pointed out) is that perhaps this is simply another demonstration of how strong Pareidolia's grip on everything is now. Not just throwing millions of affection points like USER2 once did, not just "spawning" or pretending to be special Ami in inapplicable moments, but also pertaining knowledge of an happy event during a reset whether Sensei triggered it or not. The fact that Pareidolia knows Rain King is the only thing I feel conclusive about.

Saying this is because due to the lack of understanding regarding what frog bog and rain king really mean, Pareidolia can say literally anything and wouldn't matter that much. As in, instead of frog boy, if this special Ami said "the name lamb dude/turtle guy/chicken man reminds of RAIN KING", it would make little difference to me; you can't trace any of them back to the event Rain King anyway (imagine someone who missed that event and couldn't get it just like Sensei, and went back two updates to complete the said event and still couldn't get it ).

Unless using the name frog boy specifically is Pareidolia's way to announce its presence and influence like you alluded to, like a dick measuring contest among USERS. But honestly any connection frog might've had with a certain god is currently too thin for me to claim anything with enough certainty. I need solid stuff like Callous's worm and cicada, Calm's cockroach, or Concerned's spider at least. Maybe we'll get more frog-related content in the future for further establishing, but it probably still wouldn't register well with stubborn ol' me if it's only done by having more vague metaphors or rambunctious conversations, especially when a frog can be found as early as Escape Rope, a little tangent in Ch2 with USER2's presence being much more prevalent.

"the one that sits still" and "restore the event" all sound like the description for the second god in There Is Nothing, not to mention what event comes after that is the infamous Lavender's Green.

"I am tired of collecting dust" is also a reoccurring sentence when trying to enter Mr. Tojo's room in Things Like Stairs, but this event is overall too wild for me to say anything in confidence.

posts.content_html_raw:
Don't get me wrong. Like, I've been pirating games since back when that meant taking polaroids of the paper manual to get the secret answers to the in game DRM question. So I've no problem with piracy in general and no love for DRM.

I just think that overall it's a reasonable thing to not undercut the guys primary means of profit at least until he has finished the product. If nothing else, the guy has to have some incentive to make people actually give him money instead of just playing for free. If he does not than he might just not get enough money for this whole thing to be worth his while and decide that he can spend his skills on making something else that does. And than we're out of a fun product. Of course, once the game is done all bets are off. But that goes without saying. And he'll have made enough money by than that it's fair.

Plus frankly the dev here isn't some faceless corporation like EA that can use some putting down. And as a community we can and should give support to developers by, at the very least, not completely screwing them over before they've had a chance to at least see a reasonable amount of profit or else they'll just dry up and leave us without games to steal.

I think overall the best analogy here is that we should be like parasites and not viruses. We should leach off the host for nutrients but not outright kill it. Because if the host dies we go unfed. And that's just not fun.

posts.content_html_raw:
If one day Selebus were replaced by a ghostwriter who also assumed control of the story's artistic vision, would anyone notice a difference? Is the direction LiL is heading in so unique that it couldn't be replicated by anyone else without readers noticing any deviation from its original direction?

With the way LiL is developed, there are no secrets that "happy accidents" occur, blending and weaving the interruptions and personal experiences of Selebus' life alongside the story of LiL. But how far could these diversions go before any of us notice a difference or deviation from "what Lessons in Love should be/should have been," assuming it had any vague direction or objective to begin with?

Too little flexibility yields a rigid narrative that doesn't blend well with passing times, but too much flexibility and there may not be a narrative backbone at all—no true story to tell, just whatever comes to mind at a given moment, and mindsets change by the hour. That is the sort of feeling I get with how haywire recent chapters have been, and I'm interested to see if anyone else catches a glimpse of that or if I am just reading into it too much. Maybe it's progressing as intended, or maybe there's too much improvisation, as we know.

From what I could tell, though, Selebus seems to be vague about everything regarding the narrative direction of Lessons in Love, making it impossible to decipher between character development or character deviation—apart from the financial objectives; only there are his goals made abundantly clear.

Sure, it is unique in its history and its impact, but is it unique because of Selebus' fragility, or was it unique because of what Selebus once wanted it to be? And does that still hold up with what it is today?

I feel like a question like this could be infinitely revisited since LiL is stated to be a continuously progressing narrative with no end in sight. To illustrate this, we know so little about what the foundational state of LiL is supposed to be, specifically because one of the main points of LiL is that we are not supposed to understand it. Since we cannot objectively understand many aspects of it, theoretically anything can happen to change constants we presume to understand already, and we would be none the wiser if it is intentional, a retcon, a revision, or normal progression. The fantastical nature of LiL means literally anything can occur, and it could seamlessly flow through the story or be explained away as some expected anomaly necessary to fulfill a point of the narrative we might not know about. Is that good writing or a weakness? It may be impossible to tell.

I'm particularly interested in the concept of the death of the author and supremacy of the reader. With the unique development behind LiL, the author could theoretically be replaced by anyone for a moment, and it might be impossible for us as readers to know the difference. LiL is so narratively incomprehensible that anything could happen, and we would have no choice but to accept it as if it were supposed to be there. We might not be able to identify mistakes or breaks of logic, or the feasibility of deus-ex spider-angel Gods, or characters not acting the way they should, simply because we still don't understand the 'rules' of the story or what the story should be. Or anything for that matter.

... Or maybe that's the point, though: to intentionally make trying to understand anything pointless. Kudos to Maya for not understanding anything of her world after how many years; I feel like we barely understood anything in four.

Sel has seemed rather straightforward on the plans. Harem Route -> Dark Route -> Purity Routes -> True End. In a 10 year development (according to the wiki). We're on year 4 (Chapter 4). Considering the game has also been reworked and will probably be reworked again eventually, it's likely the game will reach it's intended outcome no matter the deviation. (Unless Sel dies)

There's also still the Prequel 'Nothing Is Beautiful' and perhaps a Sequel(?) 'Grow Old. Then Die', that seem to still be in mind, and both were referenced through cameos, in the recent 'Rain King' Happy Event.

Of course, it's all a work in progress, but Sel doesn't strike me as the kind of person who'd alter the core of their vision, otherwise this would probably still be on patreon and the wizards wouldn't exist.

I'm also of the opinion that when someone tries to replicate another's work, it's usually not too hard to tell. People can't seem to help introducing part of themselves into their work, and into the work of others, hence stuff like Headcanon and Fan Fiction. There's plenty of people who'd be hoodwinked, though. (This is coming from someone who's read an obnoxious amount of comics, which tend to have so many writers, retcons, and inconsistencies, it's painful to be a fan.)

Still, no recent development in LiL has been that surprising, imo. Even New Maya has been predictable. Especially considering that Sensei likely missed her bday, which might come up soon.

I am in complete agreement with you on this. Selly designs his world this way so that whatever card he plays he can claim it's a wild card and the way he plays definitely goes by the rules. But sometimes I do feel like he is taking this a little too much, making things extra incomprehensible not because some necessities due to story reason, but because he can just do that. The truth is if you do it often enough people will drop some aspects of the game and focus on what they are "allowed to understand" (seen folks here giving up god stuff completely and only looking forward to teenager dramas, and it's completely understandable).


Despite this, however, I am mostly fine with this because I subjectively want to believe that somewhere in a plain of existence there is a LiL story with its main structure already done, all its milestones already set, and its final destination already scheduled to perfection or at least to our hearts' content so that every piece of clue one day will fall into place. For this he has to do his part in doing great articulations, and not just by using the phrase everything is connected as some sort of almighty spell when that should be your goal and not your method. As long as he nails the important elements, a few dents in the story which result from making pit stops that I personally deemed unnecessary are acceptable. You might only get a 9/10 because of it but it's ok since stuff out there that barely meets 8/10 is so far few and between already.

And by "nailing the important elements", I really hope his vision on LiL is firmly set after that massive rework. For example, I suspect his idea of how LiL should play out shifted ever so slightly after the revamp solely by judging the difference between the old and the new The Room with Clocks, where the new one introduces Maya variants sentient about how weird the world surrounding Sensei is, a second god, and Himawari a lot earlier; all relevant components with proper explanations still lacking.

So I guess what I meant by I am mostly fine, I am probably just patiently withholding judgement on a work in progress. Keep working on the project and be as convoluted as you want to. You can confuse us and we will confuse ourselves from time to time by reading too hard into an unfinished work. But there will be one day where we are able to look at this whole presentation as a hopefully cohesively weaved piece of art, and question the content in every single slide that he made a choice to include.

Anyway just a little rant; I am mostly positive for what the future holds but going into rabbit holes just happens sometimes.

posts.content_html_raw:
fdsasdf_p said:
I am in complete agreement with you on this. Selly designs his world this way so that whatever card he plays he can claim it's a wild card and the way he plays definitely goes by the rules. But sometimes I do feel like he is taking this a little too much, making things extra incomprehensible not because some necessities due to story reason, but because he can just do that. The truth is if you do it often enough people will drop some aspects of the game and focus on what they are "allowed to understand" (seen folks here giving up god stuff completely and only looking forward to teenager dramas, and it's completely understandable).
View attachment 3488094

Despite this, however, I am mostly fine with this because I subjectively want to believe that somewhere in a plain of existence there is a LiL story with its main structure already done, all its milestones already set, and its final destination already scheduled to perfection or at least to our hearts' content so that every piece of clue one day will fall into place. For this he has to do his part in doing great articulations, and not just by using the phrase everything is connected as some sort of almighty spell when that should be your goal and not your method. As long as he nails the important elements, a few dents in the story which result from making pit stops that I personally deemed unnecessary are acceptable. You might only get a 9/10 because of it but it's ok since stuff out there that barely meets 8/10 is so far few and between already.

And by "nailing the important elements", I really hope his vision on LiL is firmly set after that massive rework. For example, I suspect his idea of how LiL should play out shifted ever so slightly after the revamp solely by judging the difference between the old and the new The Room with Clocks, where the new one introduces Maya variants sentient about how weird the world surrounding Sensei is, a second god, and Himawari a lot earlier; all relevant components with proper explanations still lacking.

So I guess what I meant by I am mostly fine, I am probably just patiently withholding judgement on a work in progress. Keep working on the project and be as convoluted as you want to. You can confuse us and we will confuse ourselves from time to time by reading too hard into an unfinished work. But there will be one day where we are able to look at this whole presentation as a hopefully cohesively weaved piece of art, and question the content in every single slide that he made a choice to include.

Anyway just a little rant; I am mostly positive for what the future holds but going into rabbit holes just happens sometimes.
Click to expand...
Speaking of rabbit holes...
This reminded me of something I found... interesting:
The whole "everything is connected" thing is presumably a Pareidolia aka Concerned god thing:
https://lessonsinlove.wiki/index.ph...in_the_Forest#Event_Progression_(Spoilers!)-0
As you can see in the trivia section, and in the images that appear:
"everything is connected"
in very small letters: "-signed, the concerned"

In Theory, Pareidolia is and has been trying to make things confusing throughout the game (the rework presumably adding the Mayas, Teacher, and Shapeshifter earlier to imply this) in order to manipulate us and Sensei, into perceiving that things (and other gods/users) don't make sense, so that we'll give up and trust it with everything. It values perception:
Pareidolia - "it all comes down to perception."
Wants Sensei to think it's all in his head:
Pareidolia - "this is all in your head."
- "nothing is real."
And has been trying to get to this point for apparently a very long time:
Pareidolia - "do you have any idea how hard i had to work to get here? how long i had to wait? because i can guarantee you it would make the watermelon girl look like a tadpole gobbled up by its mother frog."

It doesn't seem to want Sensei to actually understand things (it'll have less power over him), and neither do other beings like the Shapeshifter:
Shapeshifter - "Not everything has an answer, you know! And not everything has to! So it's probably best to just never ask questions at all and accept everything you're given!"
Which presumably works with/for it.

It seems to be more or less the gaslighting god. Anything it says or is said in relation to it, should be taken with a grain of salt. It also seems to be some kind of patchwork god, made from parts of the other gods, based off the description of it's book:
Sensei - "It looks as if it's been haphazardly pieced together with different parts of other books and pages of all different sizes."
This may be the reason why Pareidolia is suddenly able to change things up and do what other gods could. It always could have. It just didn't want us to know it could, until it earned enough trust to get it's season, which it did.
TLDR: Concerned god has likely been trying to make things confusing to control the narrative.

Although, this may not be the first time Pareidolia has done this, and that might be why Kumon-mi didn't have Spring before Chapter 4. With the reintroduction of the Calm god, there's probably a reason that Sensei, connected to Pareidolia, pissed himself last update.

Or I just missed/misinterpreted something.

posts.content_html_raw:
Marie IV said:
Sure, it is unique in its history and its impact, but is it unique because of Selebus' fragility, or was it unique because of what Selebus once wanted it to be? And does that still hold up with what it is today?

I feel like a question like this could be infinitely revisited since LiL is stated to be a continuously progressing narrative with no end in sight. To illustrate this, we know so little about what the foundational state of LiL is supposed to be, specifically because one of the main points of LiL is that we are not supposed to understand it. Since we cannot objectively understand many aspects of it, theoretically anything can happen to change constants we presume to understand already, and we would be none the wiser if it is intentional, a retcon, a revision, or normal progression. The fantastical nature of LiL means literally anything can occur, and it could seamlessly flow through the story or be explained away as some expected anomaly necessary to fulfill a point of the narrative we might not know about. Is that good writing or a weakness? It may be impossible to tell.

I'm particularly interested in the concept of the death of the author and supremacy of the reader. With the unique development behind LiL, the author could theoretically be replaced by anyone for a moment, and it might be impossible for us as readers to know the difference. LiL is so narratively incomprehensible that anything could happen, and we would have no choice but to accept it as if it were supposed to be there. We might not be able to identify mistakes or breaks of logic, or the feasibility of deus-ex spider-angel Gods, or characters not acting the way they should, simply because we still don't understand the 'rules' of the story or what the story should be. Or anything for that matter.

... Or maybe that's the point, though: to intentionally make trying to understand anything pointless. Kudos to Maya for not understanding anything of her world after how many years; I feel like we barely understood anything in four.
Click to expand...
I mean, fundamentally it's not hard to understand. It's one of those games that basically try to be a subversion of the common dating sim, in both that the common goal (of picking up all the chicks) leads to your downfall, and that you really don't have much control despite having the illusion where it seems like you do. All the background stuff, while cool I guess, is ultimately just for worldbuilding and mystery. Remove all of those elements, and the theme of the story remains the exact same, which is the actual important part.

Sel isn't really replaceable because that's the entire appeal of the game, for better or for worse. It's obviously not very good writing when the author themselves is so apparent within the characters, but it also allows for a sort of intimacy and bareness that most people just aren't willing to do in their stories.
